A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flow Q-Learning by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C-D report original FQL benchmark results, online fine-tuning experiments, ablations, and runtime measurements on OGBench and D4RL.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C-D retain the original benchmark, fine-tuning, ablation, and runtime results. These include results produced by this work, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same critic, behavioral-cloning flow policy, and distilled one-step policy with identical training objectives and inference procedure. The correction to the background actor-critic equation does not change the proposed FQL algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 50 state-based and five pixel-based OGBench tasks plus 18 D4RL tasks. The same 15 offline-to-online tasks are retained, with no added domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2-3 retain the same nine offline comparators and restricted pixel-based subset; Table 4 retains the same five fine-tuning comparators. Newly cited related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendices B/E and Tables 5-7 retain the same preprocessing, architectures, hyperparameters, metrics, and evaluation procedures. For example, FQL still trains for 1M steps on state-based OGBench and 500K on D4RL/pixel-based tasks, with 50 episodes per evaluation.

E4.justification: The policy-extraction comparison in Figure 5, four ablations in Appendix C/Figure 10, and runtime analysis in Figure 11 are unchanged. No robustness test, supplementary analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight seeds for state-based tasks and four for pixel-based tasks, standard deviations in tables, and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals in plots. The exceptions for results taken from prior work are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2-4 retain all result entries, and Figures 5-12 retain the same plotted results. For example, FQL's offline antmaze-large-play score remains 84 ±7 in Table 3, and Figure 5 retains aggregate scores of 16, 29, 30, and 44 for FAWAC, FBRAC, IFQL, and FQL.

T1.justification: Equation (2) corrects the minimized actor loss's behavioral-cloning term from +alpha log pi(a|s) to -alpha log pi(a|s). The Wasserstein bound remains mathematically unchanged; its distribution symbols and equation number are updated.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and closing remarks retain the same contributions: one-step guidance avoids backpropagation through time and iterative inference while delivering strong offline and offline-to-online performance across the same 73 benchmark tasks.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly acknowledges that FQL has been evaluated only on simulated robotics tasks, without real-world evaluation. It proposes real-robot applications, potentially using a pretrained flow BC policy, as future work. The existing computational and exploration limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 removes the statement that OGBench single-task variants are available from version 1.1.0a1, reducing software-version guidance. This does not establish a change in the version actually used. Code links, implementation details, hardware information, and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 3-4 add five works concerning distillation, exploration, and action-gradient guidance: Liu et al. (2024), Li et al. (2024a), Ding et al. (2024b), Mazoure et al. (2019), and Psenka et al. (2024). This modestly expands context without redefining FQL's positioning. The formerly anonymous references are retained works with updated attribution.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits, standardized policy notation in the Wasserstein remark, publication metadata updates, and short prose additions. The main section sequence, Q&A presentation, and organization of Appendices A-E remain intact.

P2.justification: The first page gains an ICML proceedings footer, and reflow moves Equation (7) from page 3 to page 4 and shifts some figures. All 12 figures and seven tables remain, with unchanged graphical content and table structure.

improvement.justification: Correcting the BC-loss sign in Equation (2) improves mathematical accuracy, while the added references and explicit simulation-only limitation improve context and scope disclosure. These modest gains outweigh the small loss of OGBench version guidance in Appendix E.1. The algorithm and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
